hints: Look at the displacement graph at $t=0$: the particle is near negative maximum displacement, so ask whether its speed and kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ are near zero or maximum.
Recall that kinetic energy is zero at maximum displacement and maximum at zero displacement, so count how many times displacement is zero and maximum in one period $T$.
Use the fact that kinetic energy can never be negative and must peak twice for every one full displacement oscillation, then check which graph starts at zero and has four humps in time $2T$.
walkthrough: Identify the motion from the displacement-time graph: it is approximately simple harmonic with period $T$, since the pattern from one negative extreme to the next negative extreme repeats after time $T$.
State the energy rule: speed $v$ is zero at maximum displacement and maximum when displacement $x=0$, and kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ is always $\ge 0$.
Apply the starting condition: at $t=0$ the graph shows displacement near its negative extreme, so $v \approx 0$ and $E_k \approx 0$. This rules out graphs starting at a maximum.
Count the frequency: in one displacement period $T$ the particle passes through $x=0$ twice and reaches an extreme twice, so $E_k$ is maximum twice and zero twice per $T$.
Therefore in the displayed interval $2T$ there must be four kinetic energy maxima touching zero between them, all $\ge 0$. This is option D.

A.explanation: This starts at maximum kinetic energy at $t=0$ when displacement is near maximum, and it shows only one kinetic energy cycle per displacement period $T$.

B.explanation: This correctly starts at zero but shows only one kinetic energy maximum per displacement period $T$, so the frequency is not doubled.

C.explanation: This shows the doubled frequency with four maxima in $2T$, but it incorrectly starts at maximum kinetic energy when the particle is at near maximum displacement.

D.explanation: This starts at zero kinetic energy at near maximum displacement and shows two maxima per period $T$, matching zero speed at extremes and maximum speed at zero displacement.
